quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A customer wrote: 'Do you ship the oak bookcase to Ireland, and how long does it take?' The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Oak bookcase delivery to Ireland / Dear Mr Byrne, / Kind regards, Mirabel Ferro, Woodhouse Furniture). Arrange the body.
options: The shipping charge is €45, and it is shown at checkout once you enter your address.
Thank you for your interest in the oak bookcase.
Yes, we deliver to Ireland, and delivery normally takes seven to ten working days.
Please let us know if you have any other questions.
quests.hint: Answer the question in the first sentence, then add the cost detail.
quests.explanation: A good service reply answers the customer's exact question straight away. Extra information (cost) comes second because it is helpful, not central.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A customer asked whether a laptop charger is compatible with two models. Lay out the reply, which must be accurate and helpful.
options: Thank you for your question. The 65W charger works with the Zenbook 14, but it is not suitable for the Aspire 5, which needs a 90W model.

We stock the 90W charger for £34.99, and I have included the link below.

Best wishes,
Owen Pryor, Technical Support
Dear Ms Pemberton,
Subject: Re: Charger compatibility with Zenbook 14 and Aspire 5
quests.hint: Give both answers plainly, then offer a solution.
quests.explanation: When the answer is partly no, saying so clearly prevents a wrong purchase. Offering the correct product turns the limitation into service.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A customer left a vague message: 'My order is wrong.' The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Your order: we would like to help / Dear Customer, / Kind regards, Tasha Coleman). Arrange the body.
options: A photo would help if the item is damaged or incorrect.
Could you tell us your order number and what is different from what you expected?
I am sorry to hear that there is a problem with your order, and I would like to put it right.
We will reply within one working day.
quests.hint: Show empathy, ask for exactly the details required, promise timing.
quests.explanation: A specific request for information avoids repeated back-and-forth. Promising a response time reassures the customer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the email from a customer whose washing machine failed after fourteen months, when the warranty is two years.
options:
It is still within the two-year warranty. I have attached the receipt and a video of the fault, and would like to arrange a repair or replacement.

Yours faithfully,
Cynthia Bello
Subject: Warranty claim: Hydra 7 washing machine, serial HX-49128
I bought a Hydra 7 washing machine from your store on 5 April last year, and it stopped spinning on 2 June.
Dear Customer Service,
quests.hint: Product, purchase date, problem, warranty, evidence, request.
quests.explanation: A warranty claim is stronger when it establishes eligibility first. The video and receipt let the company decide without asking more questions.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Warranty claim HX-49128 / Dear Ms Bello, / Yours sincerely, Nigel Storey). Arrange the body.
options: Our engineer has reviewed them and concluded that the cracked screen was caused by an impact.
Accidental damage is not covered by the warranty, so we are unable to repair it free of charge.
We can offer a repair for £89, and I would be happy to arrange this if you would like.
Thank you for sending the photographs.
quests.hint: Explain the reasoning before the decision; offer an option.
quests.explanation: Explaining the basis of the decision makes it easier to accept. A paid repair option shows the company is trying to help despite the refusal.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Build the customer's response asking for a second review of a rejected claim.
options: Dear Mr Storey,
Subject: Request for a further review of claim HX-49128
Thank you for your explanation of the decision on my claim.

I respectfully disagree that the damage was caused by an impact, because the fault appeared while the appliance was in normal use. I would be grateful if a second engineer could examine it, and I can be available at any time next week.

Yours sincerely,
Cynthia Bello
quests.hint: Accept the message received, state disagreement politely, propose a solution.
quests.explanation: Acknowledging the explanation shows you read it. Suggesting a second inspection is a specific, reasonable next step.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email from a company informing a customer that a delivery will be late.
options: I am writing to let you know that your sofa will be delivered on Friday 20 June instead of Tuesday 17 June.

The manufacturer's lorry broke down, and we are sorry for the inconvenience. If Friday is not suitable, please reply, and we will arrange another date.

Yours sincerely,
Pauline Rowe
Subject: Update on your order 55107: new delivery date
Dear Mr Nkosi,
quests.hint: New date first, then the reason, then how to change it.
quests.explanation: The date is the information the customer needs most. Giving a reason briefly and offering flexibility shows respect.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: A customer asks for compensation for a delayed delivery that spoiled an event. Assemble the email.
options: I ordered a banner for my daughter's graduation party on 14 June, and it was promised for 9 June.
Subject: Request for compensation: order 63320, delivered two days late

It arrived on 11 June, after the event had been rescheduled, and I would like to know whether you can offer a partial refund.

Yours faithfully,
Grace Otieno
Dear Sir or Madam,
quests.hint: State the promised date, the actual date, the impact and your proposal.
quests.explanation: Describing the mismatch and its effect makes the request understandable. Asking for a partial refund is a reasonable proposal.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Lay out the reply to a customer who has chased a delayed order angrily.
options: Subject: Re: Where is my order?

It is now with the courier and will be delivered tomorrow before 6 pm. I have refunded the delivery charge, and you can track it using the link below.

Yours sincerely,
Maria Andersson
Dear Mr Chowdhury,
I understand your frustration, and I am sorry that your order 71234 is late.
quests.hint: Empathy, solution, compensation, tracking.
quests.explanation: Recognising frustration calms the tone. Giving a firm time and a refund replaces uncertainty with something concrete.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the email asking to change the size of an order that has not shipped yet.
options:
Could you change the size before it is dispatched? If it has already left, please tell me how to arrange an exchange.

Yours faithfully,
Pilar Herrera
I placed order 82019 this morning for a pair of boots in size 40, but I need size 42.
Subject: Urgent size change: order 82019, not yet dispatched
Dear Orders Team,
quests.hint: Order, change, backup plan.
quests.explanation: Speed matters here, so the order number and change come first. A fallback question avoids a second email if the order has shipped.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Size change for order 82019 / Dear Ms Herrera, / Yours sincerely, Otis Bell). Arrange the body.
options: Thank you for contacting us so quickly.
Unfortunately your order had already been dispatched when your message arrived.
You can return the boots free of charge within 30 days, and we will send size 42 at no extra cost once the return arrives.
So we cannot change it.
quests.hint: Thanks, refusal with the reason, alternative.
quests.explanation: Thanking the customer for acting quickly is polite, and explaining why the change is impossible is honest. The alternative process is the useful part.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Structure the email that adds a delivery instruction to an existing order.
options:
The flat is 12B, and the concierge is on duty until 8 pm.

Thank you,
Amina Hassan
Hello,
Subject: Delivery instruction for order 91044
Could you please add a note to order 91044 asking the courier to leave the parcel with the concierge if I am not in?
quests.hint: A small change needs a clear instruction and the needed details.
quests.explanation: A short request with the practical details (flat number, concierge hours) is easy for the company to add.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Build the email from a customer whose support ticket has had no reply for five days.
options:
I cannot access my invoices, which I need for my accounts on Friday. Could someone update me today?

Yours faithfully,
Harold Mwangi
Dear Support Team,
I opened ticket 2231 on 9 June about my account being locked, and I have not had any reply.
Subject: No reply to ticket 2231: still unresolved after five days
quests.hint: Reference, timeline, impact, request.
quests.explanation: The ticket number and dates show the delay is factual. Explaining the consequence and setting a time makes it easier to prioritise.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Ticket 2231: your account is now unlocked / Dear Mr Mwangi, / Kind regards, Deborah Rutherford). Arrange the body.
options: I have now unlocked your account and reset your password, which was sent to your registered email address.
I am sorry for the delay in replying to your ticket.
We had an unusually high volume of requests.
Please try to log in and tell me if you have any further difficulty.
quests.hint: Apologise briefly, then give the solution.
quests.explanation: A short explanation for the delay avoids sounding defensive. The solution is more important than a long apology.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the second follow-up to a business that still has not fixed a problem.
options: Subject: Second follow-up on ticket 2231: escalation requested
I have written twice about my locked account, on 9 and 14 June, and I have received no response.
Dear Support Manager,

I would be grateful if you could escalate this to someone who can help, and confirm by Friday that my account is unlocked.

Yours faithfully,
Harold Mwangi
quests.hint: Say what has been tried, what you ask, and by when.
quests.explanation: Listing dates shows a clear history. Asking for escalation with a deadline is firmer without being rude.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Change to your monthly charge from 1 August / Dear Ms Salazar, / Yours sincerely, Daniel Fisher). Arrange the body.
options: This is because of an annual price adjustment that appears in your contract.
You can find the details in section 4 of your agreement.
If you have any questions, please call us free on 0800 000 0000.
From 1 August, your monthly broadband charge will rise from £28 to £31.
quests.hint: State the change, explain, and provide contact.
quests.explanation: Customers need the amount and the date before the reason. Pointing to the contract clause shows transparency.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the customer's reply questioning the price rise.
options:
However, I read section 4 and it says increases would be limited to £2 a year. Could you please clarify how the £3 rise complies with this?

Yours sincerely,
Priya Salazar
Subject: Re: Change to my monthly charge
Dear Mr Fisher,
Thank you for the explanation of the price change from £28 to £31.
quests.hint: Acknowledge, cite the specific clause, ask a precise question.
quests.explanation: Quoting the contract makes the question difficult to ignore. Asking for clarification is firm but non-hostile.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the company's admission of an error and correction.
options: Thank you for your careful reading of the contract. You are right, and I am sorry that we applied the wrong increase.

Your monthly charge will remain £30 rather than £31, and we will credit the extra £1 for the months already billed.

Yours sincerely,
Daniel Fisher
Dear Ms Salazar,
Subject: Correction to your monthly charge
quests.hint: Acknowledge the customer's point, own the error, give correction.
quests.explanation: Agreeing plainly builds trust. Saying exactly what will change removes doubt.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email cancelling a subscription and declining a discount offer.
options: Thank you for offering a discount to keep my membership.

I appreciate it, but I have decided to cancel because I am moving abroad and will not be able to use the service. Please confirm the cancellation date and that no further payments will be taken.

Best wishes,
Marisol Vega
Subject: Re: Your offer of 30% off
Dear Anders,
quests.hint: Thank, decline firmly, give a reason, request confirmation.
quests.explanation: Being clear stops the company from making further offers. Asking for confirmation protects you from unwanted charges.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Your membership has been cancelled / Dear Marisol, / With best wishes for your move, Anders Holm). Arrange the body.
options: But I confirm that your membership will end on 30 June.
We are sorry to see you go.
If you ever return, your saved progress will still be here.
No further payments will be taken, and you can use the app until that date.
quests.hint: Confirmation, what happens, a warm close.
quests.explanation: The confirmation answers her main concern. A friendly personal ending suits a brand that wants goodwill.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Put together an email from a customer asking a company to stop marketing messages.
options: Please remove my email address, isabel.marin@example.com, from all your marketing lists.
Dear Sir or Madam,

I have unsubscribed twice, but I continue to receive weekly offers. Please confirm in writing that this has been done.

Yours faithfully,
Isabel Marin
Subject: Request to stop marketing emails
quests.hint: Instruction first, with details, then evidence of the problem.
quests.explanation: The instruction is unambiguous. Mentioning the failed unsubscribe attempts shows why you have written and supports a request for confirmation.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Assemble the email requesting an accessible seat at a theatre.
options: Subject: Wheelchair space needed: 'The Tempest', 18 October

Could you tell me which seats are available and whether there is step-free access from the street?

Yours faithfully,
Evelyn Marsh
I would like to book two tickets for 'The Tempest' on 18 October, including one wheelchair space and a seat for my companion.
Dear Box Office,
quests.hint: State the booking, the specific requirement and the information you need.
quests.explanation: Specific requirements are easier to meet. Asking about step-free access helps you plan the journey.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email requesting a large-print version of a document.
options: I am partially sighted and would like to receive the tenancy agreement in large print.
Subject: Request for a large-print copy of the tenancy agreement

Could you send it by post, or let me know if there is a digital version compatible with a screen reader?

Yours faithfully,
Mr A. Okoye
Dear Housing Team,
quests.hint: State the need and offer alternatives you can use.
quests.explanation: You do not need to give medical details. Offering two possible formats gives the organisation options.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Piece together the email requesting a quiet room at an exam centre.
options: Dear Exams Officer,
I would like to ask whether I could sit my exam on 10 June in a separate quiet room.
Subject: Request for a quiet room: exam on 10 June, candidate no. 40771

I have anxiety difficulties, and I have attached a letter from my doctor. I would be grateful to know what further evidence you need.

Yours sincerely,
Gideon Ayers
quests.hint: Request, reason, evidence, next step.
quests.explanation: A short, factual reason with evidence is usually enough. Asking what else you need shows willingness to cooperate.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Set out the email from a diner who received poor service and wants the manager to know.
options: Subject: Feedback on our visit on Saturday 21 June

The staff were pleasant, but nobody told us about the delay. We would like you to know, and I would welcome a reply.

Yours faithfully,
Elliott James
Dear Manager,
We dined at your restaurant on Saturday at 7:30 pm, and were disappointed that we waited over an hour for our main courses.
quests.hint: Facts, then balanced comment, then what you want.
quests.explanation: Naming the time and the delay keeps the message factual. Acknowledging pleasant staff shows fairness.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Re: Feedback on your visit on 21 June / Dear Mr James, / Yours sincerely, Claudia Ferretti, Manager). Arrange the body.
options: The kitchen was short-staffed that evening, but we should have kept you informed.
Thank you for taking the time to write to us.
I am sorry that you waited so long and were not told about the delay.
I would like to invite you and a guest for dinner, which will be on us.
quests.hint: Thank, apologise, explain, invite.
quests.explanation: A sincere reply includes what the business will do. The invitation is a gesture that reopens the relationship.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Arrange the email from a gym member who reports that equipment has been broken for weeks.
options: I have been a member for four years, and I am writing about the treadmills at the Westgate branch.
Dear Ms Harker,
Subject: Broken treadmills at the Westgate branch

Three of the five have displayed 'out of order' signs for over a month. Could you tell me when they will be repaired or replaced?

Kind regards,
Samuel Iwu
quests.hint: Establish credibility, state the facts, ask for a timeline.
quests.explanation: Mentioning your membership shows you are a loyal customer. Asking for a timeline invites a practical answer.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Put together the email closing a support case and asking for feedback.
options:
We will close case 7714 in seven days unless you tell us there is a problem.

If you have a moment, we would appreciate your feedback in the short survey below.

Kind regards,
Emilio Vargas
Subject: Your case 7714 has been resolved
Dear Ms Kaur,
I am glad to confirm that the problem with your invoice has been fixed, and the corrected version is attached.
quests.hint: Resolution, what happens next, request for feedback.
quests.explanation: The customer first needs to know that the issue is resolved. The closing timeline and survey are secondary.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: The subject line, greeting and sign-off are already written (Subject: Thank you for solving my problem / Dear Emilio, / Kind regards, Harpreet Kaur). Arrange the body.
options: I wanted to thank you for fixing my invoice so quickly.
You explained everything clearly and were patient with my questions.
Please pass my thanks to your manager.
It made a stressful situation much easier.
quests.hint: Thanks, reason, request to pass on.
quests.explanation: Specific compliments are valuable to service staff. Asking to inform the manager helps the agent get recognition.

quests.instruction: ARRANGE THE EMAIL PARTS INTO THE CORRECT ORDER
quests.prompt: Lay out the email from a company inviting a customer to a loyalty scheme after a resolved issue.
options: Dear Mr Adebayo,

As a thank-you, we would like to invite you to join our loyalty scheme, which gives 10% off your next purchase.

You can join using the code below before 31 July.

Best wishes,
Rebecca Hill
Subject: A thank-you for your patience
Thank you for your patience while we resolved the problem with your order.
quests.hint: Thanks, offer, action and deadline.
quests.explanation: The thanks is sincere before the offer. Ending with the instruction and date makes it easy to act.
